causal_review.next_discriminator_assessment: The passive visibilitychange recorder and health/action brackets target the missing event timing; the independent native observation targets the renderer-versus-physical gap. This is the right discriminator class, but the current proposal is not yet executable as specified: page performance.now() and driver monotonic clocks have different time origins, so correlate all phase markers and visibility events in one clock domain (preferably by having the existing panel-realm recorder accept boundary markers) or document a calibrated offset and uncertainty. Ordering can establish temporal association, not causation. Also establish the native capture API, exact Chrome-window/PID correlation, runner permission, and selected-window-only privacy behavior with a synthetic blank window before relying on a real authenticated capture; otherwise the physical-state half remains unmeasured. Keep capture passive and ensure instrumentation does not focus, reopen, or gate acceptance.
causal_review.source_to_native_limit: Source and unit tests validate sentinel classification and diagnostic fail-closed behavior only; they do not establish that native Chrome kept the side panel exposed or explain the authenticated visibility transition.
